Fuel Range Anxiety Guide

Running out of fuel in the Scottish Highlands is no joke. Know your bike's range and plan accordingly.

Typical Ranges by Bike Type

  • Adventure Bikes — 20L tank, ~250 miles. BMW R1250GS, Tiger 1200.
  • Sport Tourers — 19L tank, ~220 miles. Ninja 1000SX, Tracer 9 GT.
  • Full Dressers — 25L tank, ~300 miles. Gold Wing, K1600GTL.
  • Naked/Standards — 14L tank, ~150 miles. MT-07, Z650.
  • Dual Sport — 12L tank, ~130 miles. CRF300L, KLX300.

UK Fuel Danger Zones

Scottish Highlands (80+ miles between stations), Mid-Wales, North Pennines, and Dartmoor all have sparse fuel coverage. Read our Best Motorcycle Roads in Scotland: 15 Must-Ride Routes guide for more. Golden Rule: Fill up when you hit half tank in remote areas. Never pass a petrol station you need.
keyTakeaways: Full dressers lead on range with 25L tanks and around 300 miles between fills.
Adventure bikes manage roughly 250 miles from a 20L tank.
Naked and dual-sport bikes have the shortest range at 130 to 150 miles.
The Scottish Highlands can have 80-plus miles between fuel stations.
In remote areas, fill up at half a tank and never pass a station you need.

faq.q: How far can a motorcycle go on a full tank?
faq.a: It depends heavily on the bike. Full dressers with 25L tanks can cover around 300 miles, adventure bikes about 250, sport tourers roughly 220, while naked bikes and dual sports with smaller 12 to 14L tanks manage only 130 to 150 miles. Riding style, load and speed all affect real-world range, so treat these as guides.

faq.q: Where in the UK is fuel hardest to find?
faq.a: The Scottish Highlands are the biggest challenge, with 80-plus miles between some stations and limited opening hours. Mid-Wales, the North Pennines and Dartmoor also have sparse fuel coverage. In these areas, plan your fill-ups around the towns, carry a plan B, and do not rely on a single remote pump being open.

faq.q: How can I avoid running out of fuel on a tour?
faq.a: Know your bike's realistic range, note when your fuel warning light comes on and how far you can go afterwards, and plan stops around it. In remote areas the golden rule is to fill up when you reach half a tank rather than waiting. Never ride past a station you might need on the assumption of finding another soon.

faq.q: Does riding style affect fuel range?
faq.a: Significantly. Hard acceleration, high motorway speeds, heavy luggage, a pillion and strong headwinds all cut range, sometimes dramatically. Smooth, steady riding at moderate speeds extends it. In remote areas, easing off your pace not only stretches your fuel but also lets you enjoy the scenery, which is often the point of the ride.

faq.q: Should I carry spare fuel in remote areas?
faq.a: For the most remote routes, a small approved fuel container or a bike with a larger tank provides peace of mind, particularly on shorter-range machines. Even a litre or two can bridge the gap to the next station. Store spare fuel safely and legally, and combine it with sensible fill-up planning rather than relying on it.
